items.desc: Activists tell Australian negotiators in Antalya that countries that did little to cause the climate crisis should not have to borrow to recover from it.

items.title: Last-minute push to secure mountain agenda in COP31 outcome
items.desc: The latest draft proposes a dedicated programme on mountain regions, but Nepal wants clear commitments on climate adaptation, research and finance.

items.title: Explained: Nepal and India have revived stalled air route talks. Here’s what you need to know
items.desc: Kathmandu is pushing for two-way access to the Mahendranagar route, stalled by security concerns and strategic mistrust for years.

items.title: Dipendra’s half-century fails to lift Sudurpaschim as Lumbini restrict them to 105
items.desc: Sudurpaschim managed just 20 runs in the opening powerplay before their captain scored a fighting 52, but the Royals were bowled out of momentum and finished on 105 for eight in Qualifier 1.

items.title: ‘Death is near’: Inside the hoax bomb threats that rattled Europe’s schools and airports
items.desc: Most targets were schools in the ​United Kingdom, Ireland and Italy. But media organisations, airlines, airports, charities and private individuals were also caught up in the campaign.

items.title: Lumbini Lions and Sudurpaschim Royals eye final spot
items.desc: The winners of Qualifier 1 will advance directly to the Nepal Premier League final, while the losing side will get another chance through Qualifier 2.

items.title: Dhiraaj Rajbanshi on filming ‘Himalayan Gold’, a yarsagumba thriller, above 3,800 metres
items.desc: The director's debut film, out on Friday, explores a little-seen world of Nepal’s mountain communities. He says the story began with tales of robberies in Rukum highlands.

items.title: How individual labour permits for Europe grew 22-fold in five years
items.desc: A new study says the suspension of demand-letter verification has pushed job seekers to informal agents, exposing them to fraud, debt and exploitation.

items.title: Police seize Rs16.7 million in unaccounted cash in Lalitpur
items.desc: A team from the Kathmandu Valley Crime Investigation Office recovered the money after receiving information about a suspicious financial transaction.

items.title: Nepal gets India’s approval to import 350MW and export 56MW
items.desc: The approval allows the NEA to purchase electricity for up to 17 hours a day to meet winter demand while continuing exports from three hydropower projects.

items.title: Dusit Thani Dhulikhel hosts first-ever Cake Mixing ceremony
items.desc: The resort plans to make the celebration an annual festive tradition, bringing together guests, tourism representatives and corporate partners.

items.desc: Raj Shamani’s journey from helping revive his family’s struggling business to interviewing world leaders reflects the growing influence of India’s digital creators and the power of consistency in building an audience.

items.title: Supreme Court to hear Karki’s petition against removal on Wednesday
items.desc: The former police chief has challenged the Cabinet’s decision to remove him and appoint Manoj Kumar KC as inspector general, arguing that the move was unlawful.

items.desc: Despite how Bond has come to be characterised onscreen, Fleming’s initial open-endedness means there is still space to reimagine what Bond looks like, and even who he is.

items.title: Advocates seek sweeping changes to Nepal’s sexual violence laws
items.desc: They say the draft bill must broaden the definition of rape, clearly define consent, decriminalise consensual relationships between close-in-age adolescents, ensure equal punishment for marital rape and remove the statute of limitations.

items.title: Flood-hit Rani Mahal still awaits cleanup two months on
items.desc: Sand, gravel and debris remain scattered across the historic palace grounds, while riverbank erosion threatens its foundations and local businesses struggle with a decline in visitors.

items.title: Pokhara pushes for direct flights to Indian cities
items.desc: Local tour operators want Prime Minister Balendra Shah to use his upcoming Delhi visit to advance Nepal’s aviation interests.

items.title: Nepal considers stricter IPO rules for hydropower projects
items.desc: A draft amendment would require projects to complete at least 50 percent of construction before issuing shares, drawing mixed reactions from investors and developers.
